script.focus: the tick marks and denominator remaining fifths as we hop

intent: Demonstrate add on the number-line with values [1,2] (unit 1/5). Tutor points at: the tick marks and denominator remaining fifths as we hop

frames.caption: Start at 1/5. We are standing here; we have not hopped yet.
Hop 1 moves 1/5 forward and lands on 2/5. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started.
Hop 2 lands on 3/5. 2 hops, so 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5. Every hop was one fifth; the size of the pieces never changed, only how many.

The number line provides a distinct representation from the fraction bar, and as a guided demonstration it serves as an accessible step back.
judgement.verdict: Yes, this worked demo uses a clear number-line model to directly illustrate why adding fifths leaves the denominator unchanged without leaking the exact problem.
